summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain, consistent with her history of type 1 diabetes, gastroparesis, and chronic pancreatitis. She presented with hyperglycemia and an elevated anion gap of 23, indicating diabetic ketoacidosis. She initially refused insulin but later accepted an insulin drip, which helped close the anion gap. She declined potassium repletion and additional testing. Despite clinical improvement, she requested to leave against medical advice due to discomfort with the hospital environment and a desire to manage her care at home. She demonstrated the ability to self-administer insulin and was given 15 units of long-acting insulin upon discharge. She was discharged home with instructions to continue her insulin regimen and monitor for worsening symptoms.
problems: Diabetes with ketoacidosis, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled
